holdsWhen: Static coordinates are collected before outcome and processed identically across regimes.
Regime means and cell-level deviations are adjudicated separately.
The early perturbation is small enough not to create a new degradation mechanism.
The response derivative precedes the target horizon and is measured independently of the outcome.
The common-EOL rule and censoring policy are identical across held arms.
breaksWhen: Batch, rig, or test date is perfectly confounded with regime.
The early perturbation changes damage ordering or triggers lithium plating absent in service.
DMA fitting uses incompatible OCP curves or resistance uses inconsistent pulse timing.
Late path bifurcation or a local mechanical defect has no early electrochemical response.
Pooled rank is treated as cell-level evidence without within-regime adjudication.
transferableMethod: Use a standardized perturbation to estimate an early state-response derivative, then fit a hierarchical model with explicit regime effects and require both held-regime magnitude accuracy and within-regime ranking.
surfaceSimilarityRisk: All three problems use the word 'state', but the connection is substantive only when variables, perturbations, diagnostic derivatives, and independent outcomes can be mapped with compatible units and ordering.
minimumValidation: At least three replicated regimes, 30 untouched common-EOL targets, within-regime Spearman at least 0.50, at least 25% MdAPE improvement over the static passport, calibrated interval coverage and width, bounded calibration-cell influence, and independent implementation agreement.
